title: Plan Seasoning and the Catch-Up Minimum
content:
Desk guidance for **Patient Payment Plans**: the catch-up minimum on a past-due plan follows the plan's seasoning — how long ago the patient accepted it — and whether automatic payments are set up.

## The rule

The catch-up minimum depends on the plan's seasoning: for a plan with automatic payments set up that was accepted at least 6 whole months before today it is one quarter of the regular installment; for a plan without automatic payments that was accepted at least 6 whole months before today it is one half of the regular installment; for any other plan it is one full regular installment.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Accepted at least 6 whole months before today | Automatic payments set up on the plan | Catch-up minimum |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | One quarter of the regular installment (25 percent) |
| Yes | No | One half of the regular installment (50 percent) |
| No | Yes | One full regular installment (100 percent) |
| No | No | One full regular installment (100 percent) |

- **Seasoning** is counted in whole months from the plan's acceptance date to today.
- **Automatic payments set up** reads the plan's own automatic-payment setting, whatever the method on file.
- **Regular installment** is the regular monthly installment standing on the plan; the minimum is taken to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up.

## Hypothetical cases (regular installment 62.50)

- Accepted 7 whole months ago, automatic draws from a debit card: minimum 15.63 (one quarter of 62.50 is 15.625, rounded up at the half cent).
- Accepted 8 whole months ago, paid manually: minimum 31.25.
- Accepted 5 whole months ago, automatic draws by bank transfer: not yet 6 whole months, so the minimum is the full 62.50.
- Accepted exactly 6 whole months ago, paid manually: the plan meets "at least 6 whole months", so the minimum is 31.25.
